title: The natural proofs barrier (Razborov and Rudich)
abstract: A Lean 4 proof of Theorem 4.1 of A. A. Razborov and S. Rudich, Natural proofs (1997). If a generator G_k from k bits to 2k bits, computed by circuits of polynomial size, has hardness at least 2^(k^ε) for some ε > 0 and infinitely many k, then no P/poly-natural combinatorial property is useful against P/poly. The proof follows the paper. The generator gives Goldreich–Goldwasser–Micali functions of n variables with polynomial-size circuits, which a useful property must reject. The circuit that decides the large constructive subproperty then tells these functions apart from random functions. A hybrid argument over the levels of the tree and over the nodes of a level, with all other nodes fixed, gives a circuit of size 2^O(n) that tells one output of G_k apart from a uniform string with advantage 2^(-O(n)), which contradicts the hardness for n a small power of k.
